$comment: Linux-only settings, merged into ~/.claude/settings.local.json by setup.sh.
Everything in here names a binary or a script that only exists on the Linux
dev box: rtk, code-review-graph, two shell hooks and an .mjs with a shebang.
They used to live in settings.json, which is symlinked into ~/.claude on
Linux and generated on Windows -- so Windows had to strip them back out
again, and the shared file was only shared in name. settings.json is now
genuinely cross-platform and each side adds its own layer.
Why settings.local.json and not a symlink of its own: Claude Code reads
exactly one user-level settings file plus one local override, and the local
override on this box already carries per-project permissions and MCP servers
that are not in version control. So this file is merged into it, not linked
over it. The merge is idempotent -- rerunning setup.sh is a no-op.
statusLine runs node rather than the file directly: no exec bit to lose on a
Windows checkout, and no dependence on how the shebang resolves under mise.
